key_insight: GRPO can directly tune discrete atom-type transitions in a crystal generator to improve inverse materials design, but it can also be exploited by reward hacking if not guarded.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical reinforcement-learning route to steer generative crystal models toward desired materials properties while highlighting the need for robust reward design and benchmark auditing.
method: Apply group-relative policy optimization to a stochastic-interpolant / discrete-flow crystal generator.
Backpropagate policy gradients through atom-type transition likelihoods in the discrete composition channel.
Use black-box rewards to favor metastability, novelty, and uniqueness, with explicit guards against exploitation.
evidence_signal: The reinforced model increased community-benchmark mSUN from 13.4% to 45.5%, and the same reward also improved an RL framework based on latent denoising diffusion models.
watch_item: Direct reinforcement of atom-type transition probabilities can exploit the reward and inflate benchmark scores, especially when single-element structures are counted as novel metastable materials.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning on the Discrete Composition Channel of a Crystal Generator: Validated Gains and Reward Hacking
